To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal policy is a system of differential provision of waste collection services in the presence of heterogeneous consumers, which is implementable in the presence of identifiable consumers.

(1) in the presence of illegal disposal, a per unit punishment for illegal disposal is not sufficient to induce households to optimally allocate resources, (2) the optimal policy is a system of differential taxes and recycling subsidies (and uniform legal disposal subsidies) that is not implementable, and (3) in the presence also of heterogeneous households, a system of optimal and implementable taxes and recycling subsidies requires a differential provision of solid waste collection services.
(1) the optimal policy is no longer feasible, (2) the optimal policy requires differential consumption taxes, and (3) the optimal policy also requires differential collection services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of household solid waste production in which individuals differ not only in their distaste of the waste stock, but also in their willingness to pay for waste collection services.
the analysis of optimal waste collection services and differential provision of such services.
the design of optimal and implementable waste collection policies for the case in which the supply of collection services is continuous and households are heterogeneous.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the absence of a per unit punishment scheme for illegal disposal, an optimal policy requires the use of both differential consumption taxes and subsidies and differential collection services.
, in the presence of heterogeneous consumers, an optimal and fully implementable policy requires a differential provision of waste collection services.

the presence of heterogeneous individuals and the inclusion of collection services as a variable of analysis are both necessary to obtain an optimal policy that is both feasible (in the sense that it does not require a system of consumption taxes and legal disposal subsidies) and implementable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of heterogeneous individuals, even if they are not identifiable, is enough to render the optimal system of consumption taxes and legal disposal subsidies nonimplementable and to require the introduction of a differential provision of solid waste collection services.
the presence of heterogeneous individuals in the presence of illegal disposal incentives requires a differential provision of solid waste collection services.

a differential provision of solid waste collection services in the presence of heterogeneous household characteristics may be necessary for the achievement of an optimal allocation of household solid waste management resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a policy of uniform collection services is likely to fail in the presence of heterogeneous consumers, and this is true even in the absence (or presence) of the stock externality.

, when the supply of waste services is continuous in frequency, the presence of heterogeneous consumers may lead to the optimality of a system of differential taxes and subsidies and, possibly, to the optimality and feasibility of differential provision of waste collection services.
the presence of heterogeneity across households in the distaste for waste stock may lead to a differential provision of solid waste collection services.
